title: NFRA and Society of Auditors, Chennai organise outreach programme for Audit practiceners on Creating a Better Financial Reporting Ecosystem and improving audit quality
body_text: Continuing the series of stakeholder outreach programmes and workshops for audit practitioners, a one-day outreach programme and workshop was organised by NFRA at Chennai recently on 21 November 2026, jointly with the Society of Auditors, Chennai under its theme “Creating a Better Financial Reporting Ecosystem”. Over 200 professionals participated in the outreach programme, which had the objective of supporting audit quality. The Chennai workshop was inaugurated by Shri Nitin Gupta, Chairperson, NFRA.  Shri Gupta underscored the profession’s contribution to make India Viksit Bharat in 2047 and in safeguarding public interest and building trust in financial reporting. He said that a robust financial reporting ecosystem including audit, is instrumental in attracting capital investment. Shri Nitin Gupta emphasised the need for audit firms to keep focus on audit quality given the rapid changes in technology and continue building capacity in audit of large and complex entities. Ms. Smita Jhingran, Full-Time Member, NFRA also addressed the workshop highlighting the importance of monitoring and oversight of NFRA in improving audit quality through its annual inspections. The outreach programme included focused technical sessions on key aspects of audit practice, including Audit Strategy Documentation, Audit Sampling, Risk of Material Misstatements and Concluding the Audit. To share the regulator’s views and perspectives and obtain feedback, Chairperson NFRA, Shri Nitin Gupta and Full-Time Member, Ms. Smita Jhingran also held an open house where free and frank discussions were held and queries responded to. The workshop witnessed active and enthusiastic participation from a large number of audit parctitioners. The diverse participation facilitated meaningful interactions, exchange of perspectives and discussions on audit quality challenges across firms of varying sizes, thereby enriching the overall deliberations. *** KT/ONP
